°Obeylines $ In the *Svāyambhuvasūtrasaṅgraha*,
one should perform the ritual duties at dawn upon seeing auspicious dreams.
Upon seeing a bad dream, one should perform bathing, recitation, and fire-offerings, ending with water-libations. ||1||
Having seen such auspicious dreams as crossing to the far shore of the ocean, climbing mountains, and so forth, one shall attain success. || 2 ||
Falling from a donkey, a camel, a vehicle, or into a pit is considered inauspicious;
one should perform the expiation prescribed therein according to the nature of what was seen. || 3 ||
Having drawn a white lotus measuring either four cubits or two cubits,
one should worship there the Lord of Gods, the Sovereign, ending with the Vidyā, the Aṅgas, and the Astra-mantras.
Having also worshipped the fire and performed the triple oblation (tṛkahoma),
and when the remaining rites have been completed, one should perform the "Hand of Śiva" (śivahasta) rite.
Having smeared the right hand with fragrance using the left hand,
one should place the five [faces] beginning with Sadyojāta upon the five fingers beginning with the little finger.
Having worshipped Śiva, along with His parts, in due order upon the palm of his hand,
he should touch that disciple with that hand on the head and the heart.
Then, having consecrated [the disciple] with the Heart-mantra and worshipped him,
one should lead him into the presence of Śiva, his face covered with a cloth.
One should say to him: "My dear friend, cast this garland upon Śiva.
From the place where it falls, a name should be proclaimed, preceded by the word "Śiva. || 9 ||
In that regard, the preceptor, being self-restrained, should perform the fivefold oblation for the sake of the disciple's entitlement to the three entities, with tireless and unyielding devotion. 10.
At the conclusion of the oblation, having cut the topknot, one should offer the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti) in due order;
having thus attained the Hand of Śiva, one is here called a Samayin.
Then, having drawn [the breath] from the heart with the entire self by means of the śānta-mudrā, one should join the seeker of the subsequent state with the Gāyatrī. 12.
Once the connection with the golden seed has arisen through the act of falling under the portion of Rudra,
one should offer two full oblations prior to the rite of conception (garbhādhāna).

Then one should perform the rite of conception (garbhādhāna) according to the sequence of offerings to the words of the Brahman-mantra, using Śiva and the limbs of Śiva established in the five-word [formula]. 14.
In this manner, one should perform the Puṃsavana rite; thereafter, the Sīmantonnayana;
then the Jātakarman, and likewise the naming ceremony (Nāmakaraṇa). || 15 ||
The rite of departure, as well as the first feeding of solid food, the tonsure ceremony, the initiation rite, and the application of the girdle and the deerskin; 16.
Then, for the sake of completing the vow, having performed ten times the number of oblations prescribed,
one should perform the ritual bath, followed by the marriage ceremony and the great sacrifices.
Having performed the previously mentioned oblations with the fire-sacrifice (āhuti-homa) correctly, one by one in sequence,
the performer of the subsequent rite should offer the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti) according to the ritual procedure.
Then, one should gradually perform the Pākayajña, the Haviryajña, and the Soma-saṃsthā rites through the act of oblation,
increasing it by one, two, and three times respectively.
Then the preceptor should cause him to drink Soma, consecrated by the recitation of mantras, from a vessel made of Udumbara wood, or else with water scented with ghee.
Having performed the fire-oblation (homa) with the [mantras] beginning with Śiva for the purpose of completing the thousand-fold rite,
one should then offer the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti), which is conceived according to the principles of right and wrong conduct.
Then, by this very same procedure, having offered the sacrificial fee at the commencement of the rite,
he should cause him to enter the next stage of life, that of the forest-dweller.
Having performed the rite of renunciation and having bowed to the God,
one should say, "Forgive me, O Lord of the gods," and then dismiss him.
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, on the Consecration of the Observance, in the Svāyambhuvasūtrasaṅgraha.
